title: Effects of Wearing Progressive Addition Lens on Working Distance and Refractive Status in Adult Computer Users
brief_summary: With the increasing reliance on tablet computers and smartphones in daily life, it is important to determine whether and how the prolonged usage of these handheld digital devices influences the working habits and refractive status. This study aimed to determine the effects of wearing conventional single-vision lenses vs. new progressive addition lenses on the working distance and refractive status while playing interactive video game in Chinese pre-presbyopic adult computer users.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Hong Kong Chinese
* Computer users (computer usage \>2hours/day)
* Spherical-equivalent refractive errors between plano and -9.00D and cylindrical power ≤2.50D

Exclusion Criteria:

* Anyone with visual acuity worse than 0 logMAR, anisometropia more than 2.00D, abnormal accommodative function, wearing rigid contact lens, and a history of ocular surgery and pathology
condition: Video Game Play Using Handheld Computer
